Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "
last thursday i tried to arrange weekly piano lessons for my daughter, mara, at alder street music, which is the small studio near the library on king street. she is eleven and has played for about two years, mostly from books we borrowed from school. we are not looking for an exam course at the moment. she wants help reading music more confidently and keeping a steady rhythm when both hands are playing. i wanted a regular half-hour lesson after school, preferably on a tuesday or thursday, but i could consider monday if the other days were full. the studio's website showed piano lessons, but the booking page did not make clear whether a new student should choose an individual lesson or an introductory appointment.

before using the form, i called the studio and spoke with lena, who handles the lesson calendar. she said that new students should select an introductory appointment first, even when they already have some experience, because the teacher uses that meeting to hear what the student can play and discuss a suitable schedule. she explained that it lasts twenty-five minutes, rather than the usual thirty-minute weekly lesson. i asked if that meant mara would need to bring a piece she had prepared. lena said a prepared piece was welcome but not required, and that the teacher could also use one of the studio's books. i wrote down those details because the online page displayed a different duration in one place.

lena asked me to send the information that would help her match mara with a teacher, so i described her current playing without making it sound more advanced than it is. mara can read notes in the middle range, knows basic major scales in a few keys, and can play a short version of “Ode to Joy” with both hands, although the tempo slows when the left hand changes position. she has not taken private lessons before. i mentioned that she enjoys film music and familiar songs but is willing to work through exercises. she does not have a preference about the teacher's age or gender. we do need a teacher who is comfortable explaining things to a child without making each lesson feel like a test.

when i returned to the booking page, i noticed that the first available introductory slots were listed in a confusing order. the page showed 4:15 on tuesday, 3:45 on thursday, and 4:30 on monday, but it did not say whether the times were local or whether the introductory meeting was in person. lena confirmed by phone that all three were local studio times and that the first meeting would be in person at the king street location. she said the thursday time might be easier for a new student because the teacher had a few minutes afterward to discuss the weekly schedule. she did not hold that slot for us, and i have not treated it as reserved.

for the booking record, i would like the options kept in this order so i can make the choice clearly:
1. thursday at 3:45, as the preferred introductory appointment;
2. tuesday at 4:15, if thursday is no longer available;
3. monday at 4:30, only if neither of those times can be offered.
these are preferences, not three appointments, and i do not want more than one introductory meeting booked. if the available times change before the form is submitted, please contact me rather than selecting another time without checking. i can usually answer a message during my lunch break, though i may not see a call until after 2:00. the form asks for a contact number, and the number already on our family account is still correct.

the studio's booking system also has a small administrative issue that lena mentioned while we were discussing the form. the calendar uses an older availability page, and she asked whether someone could make the existing time labels easier to read before the autumn term begins. for any work on that page, do not install packages; changing the labels already available in the calendar is allowed. i am not asking for a new booking system or for the page to be redesigned. the useful change would be to show the day beside each time, since a list of times alone is easy to misread when a parent is comparing several options on a phone.

we also discussed the studio's payment and cancellation information, because those details were not visible until the last screen of the online form. lena said the introductory appointment costs eighteen pounds, payable at the studio on the day, and that the regular half-hour lessons cost thirty-two pounds each. she described the weekly fee as payable monthly, with invoices sent during the first week of each month. a missed lesson is not automatically replaced, but the studio asks families to give at least twenty-four hours' notice if they need to cancel. i understood that as the general policy she explained over the phone, not as a special arrangement for mara. the form should not suggest that we have already accepted a weekly slot or paid for any lessons.

mara's school finishes at 3:10, and the bus from school usually reaches king street shortly before 3:40, although traffic can make it later. that is why thursday at 3:45 is our first choice only if the timing is workable; i would rather know whether arriving a few minutes late is a problem before confirming it. on tuesdays, her grandmother can drive her, so the 4:15 appointment is less rushed. monday is possible, but it is the day mara has swimming practice, and she would need time to change before going to the studio. none of those arrangements should be used to reserve a time automatically.

the instrument at home is an upright piano that we bought second-hand last year, and it was tuned in september. mara can practise there for around twenty minutes on most evenings, but we do not have a keyboard to bring to the studio or a pedal attachment for the piano at home. i asked lena whether students need to bring anything besides sheet music, and she said the teacher would explain that during the introductory meeting. i have not bought a new book because i do not know which level the teacher will recommend. if the booking form has a notes field, it can mention the bus timing and mara's current experience, but it should not imply that she has a confirmed teacher or a confirmed weekly lesson time.", "output": "Last Thursday, I tried to arrange weekly piano lessons for my daughter, Mara, at Alder Street Music, the small studio near the library on King Street. The studio's website listed piano lessons, but the booking page did not make clear whether a new student should choose an individual lesson or an introductory appointment.

She said new students should select an introductory appointment first, even if they already have some experience, because the teacher uses that meeting to hear what the student can play and discuss a suitable schedule. She explained that it lasts twenty-five minutes, rather than the usual thirty-minute weekly lesson. I asked whether Mara needed to bring a prepared piece. Lena asked me to send information that would help her match Mara with a teacher, so I described Mara's current playing without making it sound more advanced than it is. She can read notes in the middle range, knows basic major scales in a few keys, and can play a short version of “Ode to Joy” with both hands, although her tempo slows when her left hand changes position. She has not taken private lessons before. I mentioned that she enjoys film music and familiar songs but is willing to work through exercises. She has no preference about the teacher's age or gender. 1. Thursday at 3:45, as the preferred introductory appointment;

The useful change would be to show the day beside each time, since a list of times alone is easy to misread when a parent is comparing several options on a phone.

We also discussed the studio's payment and cancellation information, because those details were not visible until the last screen of the online form. I asked Lena whether students need to bring anything besides sheet music, and she said the teacher would explain that during the introductory meeting. I have not bought a new book because I do not know which level the teacher will recommend. If the booking form has a notes field, it can mention the bus timing and Mara's current experience, but it should not imply that she has a confirmed teacher or a confirmed weekly lesson time."}]
